title: Pickled Beetroot
subtitle: Classic sweet-sharp pickled beetroot in malt vinegar
excerpt: Pickled beetroot is cooked first, then packed into jars with sweetened malt vinegar. Sliced or whole small beets both work. Ready in 1 week. Makes about three 500 ml jars.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (PG #10136); Pam Corbin, Preserves. Beetroot is cooked whole before pickling to preserve both colour and texture, slicing raw before cooking bleeds the colour.

content.text: Pickled beetroot is one of the simplest preserves,  the beetroot is boiled whole until tender, then peeled and packed into jars with sweetened malt vinegar. Cooking it whole before slicing is essential: cutting before cooking bleeds the colour into the water. Makes about three 500 ml jars.

items.prepNote: whole, unpeeled, stems trimmed to 2 cm

content.text: Put the unpeeled beetroot into a large pan of cold water. Do not cut or peel,  the skin seals in the colour. Bring to the boil and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes depending on size, until a skewer goes through the centre without resistance. Small beetroot will be done in 40 minutes; large ones need up to 70 minutes.
Drain and cool slightly. Rub off the skins under cold water,  they slip off easily. Slice into rounds 5 to 8 mm thick, or leave baby beets whole. Wear gloves to avoid staining.
Make the pickling liquor and jar

Warm the vinegar, sugar, salt, peppercorns, and bay leaves in a saucepan over low heat until the sugar dissolves. Pack the beetroot slices into hot sterilised jars and pour the warm pickling liquor over, making sure the beetroot is fully submerged. Seal immediately.

items.symptom: Beetroot is very firm in the jar
items.cause: Not cooked long enough before pickling.
items.fix: Beetroot must be fully tender before jarring, it does not soften further in the vinegar. Cook until a skewer goes through without resistance.

items.symptom: Colour bleeds into the vinegar, making it very dark
items.cause: Normal, beetroot always colours the pickling liquor.
items.fix: This is expected and fine. The liquor itself becomes a useful sharp, beetroot-flavoured dressing.

items.cause: Full malt vinegar is very sharp.
items.fix: Increase sugar to 150 g, or use a combination of half malt and half cider vinegar.

items.cause: Beetroot not quite cooked through, or cooled too much before peeling.
items.fix: Rub the skins off while the beetroot is still warm, they come off much more easily than when cold.

content.text: Ready after 1 week. Sealed: 12 months. Refrigerate once opened and use within 4 weeks.
